name: Maeve Root-Memory
loreTies: Maeve is not fully mortal and not fully tree-spirit; she remembers every Gate scar cut into Avalora. Her warnings prevent living terrain from being treated like ordinary ground.
The living world adapts and endures.
shortBackstory: Maeve Root-Memory belongs to Avalora, the older source behind human myth. Maeve is Avalora’s root-memory voice. Her silver-branch regalia, thorn records, moss-veiled cloak, crow omen marks, and calm dangerous beauty should feel like the origin behind later fae queens and druid archives.

chapters.title: Before the Gate Spoke
chapters.text: Maeve Root-Memory was important before battle records named them. As living archive of avalora, Maeve Root-Memory learned the hidden machinery beneath Avalora: who records law, who witnesses oath, who warns the living world, and who profits when warnings are ignored.

chapters.title: Faction Duty
chapters.text: Maeve Root-Memory's loyalty is tied to Tuatha culture rather than battlefield glory. Their doctrine is simple and dangerous: The living world adapts and endures. The story needs them because Titans can win fights and still misunderstand what victory costs.

chapters.title: Story Arc Tie
chapters.text: During The First Reopening, Maeve Root-Memory becomes a readable witness to campaign consequence. Their first appearance, Campaign 03: Roots Below the Gate, places them where player decisions need interpretation, warning, and memory instead of another controllable unit.

chapters.title: Conflict Wound
chapters.text: The Gate pressures Maeve Root-Memory through knowledge. It offers signs that are useful but incomplete, trying to turn witness into accomplice. Their recurring conflict is whether to reveal truth early and risk panic, or wait for proof and risk lives.

chapters.title: Dashboard Role
chapters.text: As a non-playable character, Maeve Root-Memory belongs under Characters and Character Backstories. Their profile should be read beside campaign dialogue, codex unlocks, and faction pages so every briefing feels like canon consequence, not tutorial flavor.
